newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - British generators profits to lack spark.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - British generators profits to lack spark.

text.p: British electricity generators National Power and PowerGen should see steady to potentially lower year profits when they report next week, analysts said on Friday.

National Power, which reports on Tuesday, should see pretax profits after exceptionals of 760 to 792 million stg, compared with 806 million stg previously, and pay out a total dividend of around 25.5 pence per share, up from 23 pence a year ago.

PowerGen, which itself quoted forecast ranges of 530 million to 585 million stg in a briefing note to analysts in April, should see year pretax profits of 528.1 to 592 million stg when it reports on Thursday, compared with 566 million stg a year ago.
It is expected to pay out a dividend of some 26.3 pence per share against 21 pence previously.
Analysts said there would also be interest on any comments from the companies on a one-off "windfall" tax planned by the new Labour government which swept to power two weeks ago.
"A dominating factor over the results will be the windfall tax, whether they will pay and how much," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
Labour has said the tax would be levied on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities, but has so far declined to give any further details.
Treasury secretary Gordon Brown is expected to include plans for the windfall tax in his first budget, likely to be announced in June or July.
There are also concerns in the market that the Labour government might take a look at the domestic generation market to bring in heavier regulation or increase competition, analysts said.
"We'll be interested to see how they perceive competition developing, with new entrants and new plants due to come onstream," the analyst said.
The two generators might also give some indications on progress of international operations, analysts said.
In addition, analysts will be looking for indications on future strategy of the two companies.
"National Power seems to have a clear and determined strategy of returning value to shareholders while PowerGen seems to be keeping its powder dry," the analyst said.

Both National Power and PowerGen saw bids for regional electricity companies Southern and Midlands respectively blocked by the government last year. -- Jo Winterbottom, London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
